prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE production sprite on a genuinely transparent background for a winter-outfit Alice Live2D character. Image 1 (existing parts atlas) is PRIMARY rendering style, book design, black glove and dark slate-purple sleeve palette. Image 2 (approved complete character keyframe) is reference ONLY for a convincing one-hand supporting grip under an open book. Do not draw a character or a head. Draw ONLY an open antique muted plum hardcover book with understated gold corner ornamentation and ivory page blocks, plus ONE attached black leather gloved hand supporting it from beneath. This is an intentionally CONNECTED book-and-hand prop: palm visibly bears the bottom of the central spine, four fingers together and naturally curved around the lower front cover, thumb braces the side/back of the spine. Fingers lie against the cover and support the book's weight; no open V-shaped hand, no splayed fingers, no hand hanging by fingertips, no hand floating away from the book, no extra hands. The wrist emerges diagonally down toward VIEWER-LEFT, representing the character's arm on viewer-left. A short black fur cuff and a very short dark slate-purple sleeve stub extend from that wrist; leave a clean hidden attachment end for the animated forearm. Keep the hand slender and correctly proportioned to the book (palm width around one fifth book width), realistic finger joints, not a claw. The open book seen from in front of the reader has outer covers toward viewer and a shallow V around 135 degrees. Landscape book width-to-height around 1.6. Composition: centered book in the upper two thirds of a square canvas; attached supporting hand beneath the lower middle, wrist/cuff diagonally toward lower-left; generous transparent margin around everything, no clipping. Clean delicate anime linework and soft painted shading, subdued dark colours matching image 1. No lettering, no face, no torso, no second hand, no separate pieces, no background, no checkerboard baked in. Preserve actual alpha transparency. Need the whole silhouette of book, all fingers, wrist and cuff visible. The book and gripping hand move as one rigid part, with the sleeve to be connected separately later.
usage: A single connected book, supporting palm and cuff; forearm attaches to the cuff anchor so the grip cannot slide.
